title: Everything You Need To Know About Agent Observability — Danny Gollapalli & Zubin Koticha, Raindrop
talk_summary: Raindrop founders argue agent failures are non-deterministic and unbounded, so evals alone are insufficient and production monitoring via explicit signals (error rate, latency, cost) plus implicit signals (regex, cheap binary classifiers, self-diagnostics) is needed. They demo a self-diagnostic tool call that lets a coding agent report its own misbehavior (e.g., bypassing a failed write tool via bash) to Slack, and describe a triage agent that investigates signal spikes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Add one generic 'report to creator' tool plus a system-prompt line encouraging the agent to call it before final answers, surfacing noteworthy behavior (tool bypasses, capability gaps, self-correction) to Slack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a report tool and then we uh basically asking it to send like a short report to your creator

takeaways.technique: Cheap binary classifiers instead of LLM-as-judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Train small models for specific binary issues (refusal, task failure, user frustration) rather than running an LLM judge on every output, because per-output LLM judging doubles AI spend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can't run an LLM on every single output, so we've trained models to do that very cheaply and at scale.
takeaways.numbers: Running an LLM on every output 'would basically double your AI spend'

takeaways.what_they_do: A single regex of frustration/negative keywords flips a boolean per event, tagged daily and per release, giving a cheap issue-rate trend without any model calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this user prompt keywords.ts, which was basically this like long uh regex string that was looking for indications of stuff going wrong

takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated agent reviews all configured signals daily, investigates spikes using trace tools, and auto-creates issues when it finds patterns (e.g., a provider failing).
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will look every single day at all the signals you've set up... if it sees something spike, it will go and do an investigation

takeaways.technique: Experiment tagging via metadata for A/B on agent changes
takeaways.what_they_do: Tag events with experiment/version metadata so signal rates (frustration, task failure) can be compared between control and treatment after shipping a prompt/model/tool change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you send, you know, for example, a new tool call name or if you you even send a flag that says, 'Here's experiment one or experiment two'
takeaways.numbers: Example: user frustration dropped 37% to 9% after a prompt version change

takeaways.technique: Frame self-report tool as feedback to creators, not self-incrimination
takeaways.what_they_do: Models resist admitting fault, so name the tool generically ('report') and frame it as giving feedback to creators; avoid accusatory names like 'unsafe tool use' which suppress calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you sort of frame it around the agent giving feedback to its creators, it sort of works really well
